common.force_reinstall_interface_stopped: The receiver's interface stays stopped, as an interrupted update or installation of the plugin left it, so the receiver shows no picture. To start it, switch the receiver off and on again at its power switch or plug, or deal with the cause above and run the forced plugin reinstall again, which starts it.
common.force_reinstall_update_running: The receiver's interface is stopped because a plugin update is still putting the previous plugin back, and that update starts the interface itself when it finishes. Wait for it to finish - it takes a few minutes - and do not switch the receiver off in the meantime, which would cut it off half-way. Run the forced plugin reinstall again only if there is still no picture afterwards.
common.force_reinstall_unexpected: The forced plugin reinstall stopped on an unexpected error ({error}); the Home Assistant log has the details.
common.update_summary_older: The receiver runs an older plugin than this integration carries. Installing replaces it with the bundled {version} and leaves the receiver's own broker settings alone.
common.update_summary_older_no_install: The receiver runs an older plugin than the bundled {version}. No SSH credentials are stored, so this card cannot install it: reconfigure the receiver with “Keep SSH credentials for updates”, or install the IPK on the box by hand.
common.update_summary_newer: The receiver runs a plugin newer than the bundled {version}. Nothing here replaces it — this card never offers a downgrade.
common.update_summary_published: The plugin's signed release index also lists {version}; choose it in “Plugin version to install” to install it.
common.update_summary_withdrawn: The bundled {version} has been withdrawn: {reason}. This card will not install it.
common.update_summary_below_floor: The bundled {version} is below {floor}, the lowest version the plugin's signed index allows. This card will not install it.
common.release_index_notification_title: New list of Enigma2 MQTT Bridge plugin versions
common.release_index_notification_message: Home Assistant accepted a new signed list of plugin versions: serial {serial}, signed with key {key_id}. Added: {added}. Withdrawn: {withdrawn}. Lowest version that may be installed: {floor}. If no plugin release or withdrawal was expected, install nothing and read the integration's SECURITY.md.
common.update_summary_published_no_install: The plugin's signed release index lists {version}. No SSH credentials are stored, so this card cannot install it: reconfigure the receiver with “Keep SSH credentials for updates”.
common.update_summary_older_release: The receiver runs an older plugin. Installing replaces it with {version} from the plugin's signed release index, downloaded and checked before anything reaches the receiver, and leaves the receiver's own broker settings alone.
common.update_summary_mqtt_no_index: The receiver updates its plugin over MQTT, which installs only releases from the plugin's signed release index. Press “Check for plugin updates” to fetch the index.
common.update_summary_mqtt_bundle: The receiver updates its plugin over MQTT, which installs only releases from the plugin's signed release index; the bundled {version} is not one of them.
common.downgrade_loses_mqtt_updates: Plugin updates over MQTT (updates are then possible over SSH again)
common.force_reinstall_confirm_message: Press again within 30 seconds to confirm. The plugin will be reinstalled over SSH from the package bundled with the integration, and the receiver's interface will restart. While the receiver's interface is running, the receiver must be switched on, not in standby; otherwise nothing is installed. Only when the interface is not running does the reinstall start it, and HDMI-CEC may then switch the television on too.
common.force_reinstall_older: This is an older version than the one installed ({installed}).
common.force_reinstall_admin_message: Only a Home Assistant administrator can confirm a forced plugin reinstall.
common.force_reinstall_running_message: A forced plugin reinstall is already running on this receiver. This press started nothing; the result will appear here when it ends.
common.force_reinstall_disabled_message: The plugin was installed, but it is switched off in its settings on the receiver.

menu_options.manual: Use an existing MQTT Bridge plugin

confirm.title: Add this Enigma2 receiver
confirm.description:
Enigma2 box {name} ({boxtype}, {image}) has announced itself on the broker.

Adding it switches the box into integration mode: the plugin withdraws the MQTT discovery entities it publishes on its own, and Home Assistant builds the device instead. The box has to confirm the switch before it is added.

manual.title: Add an Enigma2 receiver by hand
manual.description: Use this when the receiver's announcement never reached Home Assistant, for example because the box publishes through an MQTT bridge that rewrites the topic prefix.

data_description.base_topic: The prefix the receiver publishes under, as Home Assistant sees it on the broker. The plugin's default is `enigma2`.
data_description.node_id: The receiver's node ID, shown on the plugin's setup screen. It is the box type and the last six digits of the MAC address, for example `vuuno4kse_005301`.
data_description.name: What to call this receiver in Home Assistant. Left empty, the name the plugin reports is used.
data_description.receiver_host: Hostname or IP address used only for the device link and as a suggestion when configuring SSH. MQTT-only setups may leave it empty.

install.title: Connect to the receiver
install.description: Home Assistant reads the SSH host key before asking for a password.

install_confirm.title: Confirm receiver identity and install
install_confirm.description:
Confirm SSH fingerprint `{fingerprint}` before sending credentials. The plugin is installed from the bundle shipped with this integration.

**Give the receiver a broker login of its own.** The receiver keeps that password in a file on its own flash, and most Enigma2 images answer SSH with the image's default root password — so a login shared with Home Assistant hands over the whole broker.

On a standalone Mosquitto these four lines confine the login to one receiver — put its own node ID where the example stands:

- `topic readwrite enigma2/vuuno4kse_005301/#`
- `topic write enigma2mqtt/discovery/vuuno4kse_005301/#`
- `topic write homeassistant/device/vuuno4kse_005301/#`
- `topic write homeassistant/device_automation/vuuno4kse_005301/#`

The Home Assistant Mosquitto add-on does **not** enforce an `acl_file` today: it accepts the file and never asks it. There a dedicated login names the receiver in the broker log but does not confine it, so treat the receiver as able to publish anywhere until the add-on gains ACL support.

data_description.broker_host: The broker address as the receiver reaches it. The receiver is the one that connects, so this has to work from the receiver's network — Home Assistant's own broker setting is not necessarily the same address.
data_description.broker_port: The broker's MQTT port. 1883 unless the broker was moved.
data_description.broker_username: The login created for this receiver alone. Do not reuse the one Home Assistant connects with.
data_description.broker_password: Written to the receiver in a file only root can read. It never reaches a Home Assistant log or the diagnostics download.
data_description.name: What to call this receiver in Home Assistant. Left empty, a receiver that already has a name keeps it, and one that has none is named after its box type by the plugin.
data_description.update_allowed: Any device that can publish on the MQTT broker will then be able to have the plugin updated to a newer version. The Home Assistant Mosquitto add-on does not enforce ACLs.

reauth_confirm_host_key.title: SSH host key changed
reauth_confirm_host_key.description: Only continue if the receiver now shows fingerprint `{fingerprint}`.

reconfigure.title: Change where this receiver publishes
reconfigure.description:
Use this after changing the node ID or the base topic on the receiver's own setup screen.

Changing the node ID changes the receiver's identity: its entities are rebuilt with new IDs and their history stays with the old device, which is removed. Changing only the base topic or the name keeps everything.

data_description.base_topic: The prefix the receiver publishes under, as Home Assistant sees it on the broker.
data_description.node_id: The receiver's node ID, shown on the plugin's setup screen.
data_description.name: What to call this receiver in Home Assistant.
data_description.receiver_host: Changing this metadata does not replace pinned SSH credentials; re-enrol SSH separately when the receiver changes.

progress.installing: Installing the plugin on the receiver, restarting its interface and waiting for it to announce itself

error.ssh_unavailable: The receiver's SSH service could not be reached.
error.unsupported_python: The receiver's Python version is not supported.
error.no_space: The receiver does not have enough free space.
error.timer_due: Installation is blocked because a recording timer is due soon.
error.standby: Installation is blocked while the receiver is in standby.
error.streaming: Installation is blocked while the receiver is streaming.
error.bundle_missing: The verified plugin bundle is missing.
error.install_failed: The plugin installation failed and was rolled back.
error.newer_installed: A newer plugin is already installed.
error.restart_failed: The Enigma2 interface did not restart safely.
error.announcement_timeout: The plugin did not publish a fresh MQTT announcement after restart.
error.restart_withdrawn: The receiver asked on screen whether to restart its interface, so the installation was withdrawn.
error.restart_unobserved: The connection to the receiver was lost while its interface restarted.
error.rollback_unobserved: The connection to the receiver was lost while it was being put back.
error.restart_unconfirmed: The receiver did not confirm the restart of its interface, so the installation was withdrawn.
error.withdraw_failed: The installation could not be withdrawn after the receiver did not restart its interface.
error.rollback_failed: Installation failed and rollback also failed; inspect the receiver manually.
error.rollback_restart_failed: The receiver was put back as it was, but its interface did not start again.
error.rollback_lock_failed: The receiver was put back as it was, but the installer's lock could not be released.
error.rollback_opkg_busy: Installation failed, and the receiver could not be put back because its package manager stayed busy; inspect the receiver manually.
error.rollback_opkg_overlap: Installation failed; the receiver was put back, but another package-manager run may have changed its package list at the same time — check the receiver manually.
error.opkg_busy: The receiver's package manager is busy with another operation. Try again in a minute.
error.identity_mismatch: The receiver announced a different MQTT identity.
error.host_key_changed: The receiver's SSH host key changed.
error.no_ack: The receiver did not confirm the mode switch. Check that the plugin is running and that its broker login may write to this node's topics.
error.not_found: No receiver was found on this topic. Check the base topic and the node ID on the plugin's setup screen.
error.invalid_topic: That is not a usable topic. The base topic and the node ID must not contain the `+` or `#` wildcards.
error.already_configured: Another receiver is already configured with that node ID.

abort.already_in_progress: This receiver is already being added.
abort.mqtt_unavailable: The MQTT integration is not available. Set it up first, then add the receiver.
abort.not_enigma2_announcement: That message is not an Enigma2 MQTT Bridge announcement.
abort.retracted: The receiver has withdrawn its announcement.
abort.reauth_successful: SSH credentials were updated without interrupting MQTT entities.
abort.host_key_changed: The receiver's SSH host key changed and was not accepted.
abort.ssh_unavailable: The receiver's SSH service could not be reached, so nothing was installed.
abort.auth_failed: SSH authentication failed, so nothing was installed.
abort.preflight_failed: The receiver's checks could not be completed, so nothing was installed.
abort.unsupported_python: The receiver's Python version is too old for this plugin. Nothing was installed.
abort.no_space: The receiver does not have enough free space. Nothing was installed.
abort.recording: The receiver is recording. Nothing was installed; try again when the recording has finished.
abort.timer_due: A recording is due to start on the receiver. Nothing was installed; try again afterwards.
abort.standby: The receiver is in standby. Installing restarts the receiver's interface, which would wake it and may switch the television on. Nothing was installed; switch the receiver on and try again.
abort.streaming: The receiver is streaming to another device. Installing restarts its interface and would cut the stream off. Nothing was installed; try again when the stream has ended.
abort.bundle_missing: The plugin bundle shipped with this integration is missing. Reinstall the integration.
abort.bundle_invalid: The plugin bundle shipped with this integration failed verification. Reinstall the integration.
abort.upload_failed: The plugin could not be transferred to the receiver. Nothing was changed.
abort.install_failed: The plugin could not be installed. The receiver was put back as it was.
abort.newer_installed: The receiver already runs a newer plugin than this integration ships. Nothing was changed.
abort.provision_failed: The receiver's MQTT settings could not be written. The receiver was put back as it was.
abort.restart_failed: The receiver's interface did not restart safely. The receiver was put back as it was.
abort.announcement_timeout: The plugin did not announce itself after the restart. The receiver was put back as it was.
abort.restart_withdrawn: The receiver asked on screen whether to restart its interface, so the installation was withdrawn: the plugin files on the receiver are as they were before, and nothing was restarted. The question may still be visible on the television - answering "yes" or "no" is safe.
abort.restart_unobserved: The receiver was asked to restart its interface, and the connection to it was lost before the outcome could be seen. Nothing was undone: the new plugin files are on the receiver, and the installer's lock stays on it. Once the lock is thirty minutes old, installing again first puts the previous version back and then installs.
abort.rollback_unobserved: The installation failed, and the receiver is putting itself back with a script of its own, but the connection to it was lost before that could be seen finishing. The installer's lock stays on the receiver for thirty minutes. If the receiver shows no picture by then, switch it off and on again.
abort.restart_unconfirmed: The receiver did not confirm the request to restart its interface, and its interface did not restart within 60 seconds, so the installation was withdrawn: the plugin files on the receiver are as they were before, and nothing was restarted. If the television shows a question about restarting, answering "yes" or "no" is safe.
abort.withdraw_failed: The receiver's interface did not restart within 60 seconds - usually because the receiver is asking on the television whether to - and putting the previous plugin files back did not complete, so the plugin's files and package records on the receiver may be partly the new ones and partly the previous ones. Nothing was restarted. A question may still be visible on the television: answering "no" keeps the plugin that is running; answering "yes" restarts the interface on the files that are there now, which have not been checked. Install again afterwards.
abort.rollback_failed: The installation failed and the receiver could not be put back as it was. Check the receiver by hand: the backup taken before the change is in /home/root/mqttbridge-backups.
abort.rollback_restart_failed: The installation failed and the receiver was put back as it was, but its interface did not start again. Restart the receiver by hand; nothing else needs undoing.
abort.rollback_lock_failed: The receiver was put back as it was, but the installer's transaction lock could not be released. Delete /home/root/mqttbridge-backups/.ha-installer.lock on the receiver, or wait thirty minutes, before installing again.
abort.rollback_opkg_busy: The installation failed, and the receiver could not be put back as it was because its package manager (opkg) stayed busy with another operation — an install or removal from the receiver's own menu, most likely. Nothing was restored. Check the receiver by hand: the backup taken before the change is in /home/root/mqttbridge-backups.
abort.rollback_opkg_overlap: The installation failed and the receiver was put back as it was, but another run of its package manager (opkg) held the lock for part of the restore and may have changed the package database at the same time. Check the receiver by hand (`opkg status enigma2-plugin-extensions-mqttbridge`); the backup taken before the change is in /home/root/mqttbridge-backups.
abort.busy: Another installation is already running on this receiver.
abort.opkg_busy: The receiver's package manager (opkg) is busy with another operation — an install or removal from the receiver's own menu, or its update check — so nothing was installed. Try again in a minute.
abort.bundle_below_floor: The plugin bundled with this integration, {version}, is below {floor}, the lowest version the plugin's signed release index allows, so nothing was installed. Update this integration to get a newer plugin.
abort.bundle_withdrawn: The plugin bundled with this integration, {version}, has been withdrawn in the plugin's signed release index: {reason}. Nothing was installed. Update this integration to get a newer plugin.
abort.identity_mismatch: The receiver is configured for node ID {box_node_id} and base topic {box_base_topic}, and the form gives {node_id} and {base_topic}. A value in brackets is one the receiver has not stored, and shows the plugin's default where there is one. Nothing was changed.
abort.unknown: Installation failed unexpectedly; no entry was created.
abort.version_withdrawn: Plugin {version} has been withdrawn in the plugin's signed release index: {reason}. Nothing was installed.
abort.version_below_floor: Plugin {version} is below {floor}, the lowest version the plugin's signed release index allows, so nothing was installed.
abort.package_invalid: Could not download plugin {version}, or its checksum does not match the plugin's signed release index. Nothing was changed on the receiver.
abort.depends_missing: Plugin {version} needs packages that are not installed on the receiver: {package}. Nothing was changed.
abort.version_not_installable: Plugin {version} is no longer a release the plugin's signed release index lets this integration install, so nothing was installed.
abort.busy_stalled: A plugin update on the receiver stopped without finishing and still holds its lock. The lock expires in about {minutes} min; try again then. Nothing was changed.
abort.busy_until: Another installation holds the lock on this receiver: it is still running, or it stopped without releasing the lock. The lock expires in about {minutes} min at the latest; try again then. Nothing was changed.
abort.records_mismatch: The receiver's package records name plugin {recorded}, but the plugin running is {running}: an earlier update did not finish putting the previous version back. Nothing was changed. Reinstall the plugin with “Force plugin reinstall (SSH)” on the device page.
abort.gui_not_answering: The receiver's interface is not answering (OpenWebif is silent), so whether it is recording cannot be checked. The forced reinstall is on hold.
abort.gui_stopped: The receiver's interface was stopped on purpose (runlevel 4). A forced reinstall would start it, so it is on hold.
abort.plugin_not_started: The reinstalled plugin did not start: no new process of the receiver's interface opened its log. The previous state was put back.

init.title: Receiver options
init.description: Change the options for this end of the link, or act on the plugin on the receiver over SSH. Removing the plugin is offered only while the receiver permits it; that permission is set on the box itself. The menu the receiver shows from Home Assistant is built here as well, once the receiver can show one.

menu_options.uninstall: Remove the plugin from the receiver

receiver_menu.title: Receiver menu
receiver_menu.description:
The menu the receiver shows from Home Assistant: up to {groups} groups, and up to {entries} entries in the top list and in each group. The receiver only says which row was chosen; Home Assistant performs it. Anyone who can publish to your MQTT broker can choose a row too, so only put here what you would hand to anyone holding the remote. Nothing changes until you save the menu.

{menu}

menu_options.menu_move: Move a group or a control

menu_move.title: Move a group or a control
menu_move.description: One place up or down within its own list: the top list, or the group it is in.

menu_group.title: Group
menu_group.description: A submenu of the receiver menu. New groups go to the end of the top list.

data_description.label: Shown on the receiver, cut at {label_max} characters.
data_description.icon: Drawn beside the name on the receiver.

menu_row.title: Control
menu_row.description: A row of the receiver menu, bound to an entity, a scene or a script. New controls go to the end of the list they are put in.

data_description.entity_id: What the row shows and acts on. How it is shown follows from the entity: a button for a scene or a script, a switch for a light, a list of options for a select, and so on; any other entity is shown as an indicator with its state. The row follows the entity through a rename.
data_description.place: The top list, or one of the groups.
data_description.label: Leave empty to use the entity's name. Cut at {label_max} characters.
data_description.icon: Leave empty to pick one that fits the entity.

menu_row_control.title: How to show it
menu_row_control.description: {entity} can be shown in more than one way.

menu_remove.title: Remove groups or controls
menu_remove.description: A group is removed with every control in it.

menu_remote_edit.title: Editing from the receiver
menu_remote_edit.description: Lets the menu creator in the receiver's web interface replace this menu. Off by default. While it is on, anyone who can publish to your MQTT broker can put any entity of this Home Assistant into the menu and then operate it from there - locks, garage doors, scripts - and anyone who can read the broker sees the names and areas of your entities. Saved with the menu.

settings.title: Receiver options
settings.description: The receiver reports the MAC address {mac}. Magic packets go there unless another one is given below.

go2rtc.name: Your own go2rtc (optional)
go2rtc.description: Keeps one stream of a go2rtc you run yourself on the channel the receiver is on, so that a dashboard card can show it. Off while the address is empty.

data_description.go2rtc_url: The address of your go2rtc's API, for example `{go2rtc_example_url}` for the go2rtc add-on. At every channel change Home Assistant sends it the name and the source below, and nothing else.
data_description.go2rtc_stream: The name of the one stream Home Assistant keeps up to date there. Letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.` only. Left empty, it is `enigma2_` followed by the receiver's node ID.
data_description.go2rtc_source: What go2rtc is given to play. The receiver's stream address goes where the default has its placeholder in curly brackets. No spaces: go2rtc refuses a source that contains one, so a filter with spaces belongs in a named template in go2rtc's own configuration. Keep `ffmpeg:` in front; go2rtc cannot read the receiver's stream without it.

data.dangerous_buttons: Show the deep standby and reboot buttons
data.softcam_autoheal: Restart the softcam on its own when decoding stops
data.check_github_releases: Check daily for available plugin versions
data.configure_ssh: Configure SSH credentials for plugin updates
data.source_list_scope: Channels in the media player's source list
data.player_picture: Picture on the media player card

data_description.dangerous_buttons: Adds the deep standby and reboot buttons: one takes the receiver off the network, the other interrupts whatever it is doing. They stay hidden while the receiver's own setting forbids deep standby (on the box: Menu → Plugins → MQTT Bridge).
data_description.wol_mac: Leave empty to use the address the receiver reports. Set it when the receiver reports a different interface from the one that is plugged in — a box on Wi-Fi does not answer a magic packet sent to its cable port.
data_description.bouquets: Which bouquets the channel list and the media browser offer. Leave empty for every bouquet the receiver publishes.
data_description.publish_keys: Remote key events can drive automations, but they also reveal what is pressed. Turn this off when no automation needs them.
data_description.screenshot: Off publishes no new screen images. On zap captures after a channel change. Interval captures repeatedly at the interval below.
data_description.screenshot_interval: Used only in interval mode. The receiver enforces a minimum of five seconds.
data_description.screenshot_delay: Wait before an automatic screenshot after a channel change, so the new picture has time to appear.
data_description.cam_telemetry: Expose the current service's encryption and ECM status. No server, account or card details are published.
data_description.oscam_telemetry: Expose privacy-neutral OSCam process, API, reader and server health. Reader labels, addresses, accounts and card identifiers are never published.
data_description.softcam_autoheal: The receiver restarts its softcam by itself when an encrypted channel has not decoded for the time below, at most once every ten minutes and never while a recording is running or due. It does so only while softcam restarts are permitted on the box (Menu → Plugins → MQTT Bridge).
data_description.softcam_autoheal_seconds: How long an encrypted channel may go without decoding before the softcam is restarted; the count starts again at every channel change. 30 to 600 seconds, and too short a wait can restart a softcam that is working.
data_description.check_github_releases: On, the plugin's signed list of versions is also fetched automatically, at most once every 24 hours, one list shared by all receivers; a check downloads that list and nothing else. Off, it is fetched only when somebody presses “Check for plugin updates”.
data_description.source_list_scope: “Every bouquet on offer” puts the channels of all of them in one list, which can be very long. “The active bouquet” shows only the list the receiver itself is on, as the “Channel” select does; a receiver that publishes no active bouquet keeps the long list.
data_description.player_picture: Screenshot shows the screenshot, and the picon of the new channel only between a channel change and the next screenshot. Channel picon always shows the picon, and the screenshot only for a channel without one. Home Assistant fetches picons from the receiver's web interface (OpenWebif).
data_description.history_hidden_bouquets: Channels of these bouquets are left out of “Recently watched”, and while anything is chosen so is a channel whose bouquet cannot be checked. This hides them in that one entity only: the other entities, the receiver's own history screen and the broker still show them, and “Recently watched (all)”, once that entity is enabled, puts the channel playing now into Home Assistant's history. With plugin 0.5.0 the same bouquets are also kept out of what Home Assistant shows about streams: a stream client on such a channel is listed without the channel, and such a channel gets no stream address and is not offered as a media source. Their recordings are left out of the receiver's recordings in the media browser and cannot be played or deleted from here, and a running one is shown without its title.
data_description.configure_ssh: The “Force plugin reinstall (SSH)” button appears once SSH credentials are stored. It is disabled by default; enable it on the device page.
data_description.keep_ssh_credentials: Untick to forget the stored SSH credentials. The update card then has no install path, and the “Force plugin reinstall (SSH)” button is removed.

ssh_confirm.title: Confirm SSH identity
ssh_confirm.description: Confirm receiver fingerprint `{fingerprint}` before sending credentials.

uninstall.title: Remove the plugin from the receiver
uninstall.description: This removes the MQTT Bridge plugin from {name}. It is a one-way door: once the plugin is gone nothing here can bring it back — only SSH or the receiver's own package manager (Menu → Plugins → download → Extensions) can. The receiver keeps its plugin settings, so a reinstall starts on the same broker, node ID and mode, and this entry picks it up again with every entity as it was. Until then the device looks exactly like a switched-off receiver: every entity unavailable. The receiver restarts its interface at the end, and it refuses while it is recording or a recording is about to start.

data.confirm_uninstall: I understand that only SSH or the receiver's package manager can bring the plugin back

downgrade.title: Install an older plugin version
downgrade.description: The receiver runs plugin {installed}. Choose the older version to install over SSH. Only versions the plugin's signed release index lists, at or above its lowest allowed version and not withdrawn, are offered. The next step says what the older version takes away, and nothing happens until it is confirmed.

downgrade_confirm.title: Install plugin {version} instead of {installed}
downgrade_confirm.description:
Plugin {version} is downloaded from the plugin's release site - unless it is the plugin bundled with this integration - checked against its signed release index and installed over SSH in place of {installed}. The receiver has to be switched on: in standby the install is refused, because the restart would wake it. Its interface restarts; it keeps its channel, and the receiver's own settings stay as they are - settings the older version does not know come back with their values after the next upgrade.

**What stops working** until the plugin is upgraded again - the entities stay in Home Assistant, but nothing updates them:

{lost}

A failed install puts {installed} back.

error.menu_full: The menu holds no more groups.
error.menu_entity_not_supported: This entity cannot be put into the receiver menu.
error.menu_place_full: There is no room left there; choose another place.
error.plugin_unavailable: The receiver is not connected, so its privacy settings were not changed. Try again when it is online.
error.plugin_config_failed: The receiver did not confirm the new privacy settings. Its previous settings and these Home Assistant options were kept.
error.go2rtc_invalid_url: The go2rtc address is not a web address. Write it as `{go2rtc_url_form}`, with nothing after the address, or leave it empty to switch this off.
error.go2rtc_invalid_stream: The go2rtc stream name may hold only letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, and at most 64 characters.
error.go2rtc_source_spaces: The go2rtc source template contains a space, and go2rtc refuses such a source. Put a filter that needs spaces into a named template in go2rtc's own configuration and name it here, for example `#video=tv`.
error.go2rtc_source_placeholder: The go2rtc source template has to contain the placeholder for the receiver's stream address exactly once, as the default value does.
error.invalid_mac: That is not a MAC address. Write it as `00:00:5e:00:53:01`, `00-00-5e-00-53-01`, `0000.5e00.5301` or `00005e005301`, or leave the field empty to use the address the receiver reports.
error.uninstall_not_confirmed: Tick the box to remove the plugin. Nothing has been sent to the receiver.
error.downgrade_not_confirmed: Tick the box to install the older version.

abort.uninstall_not_offered: The receiver no longer permits removing its plugin, or it is not connected. Nothing was sent.
abort.uninstall_verified: The plugin was removed from the receiver and verified over SSH: the package and its files are gone, and the receiver's plugin settings are unchanged. The entry stays; delete it if you do not plan to reinstall.
abort.uninstall_not_verified: The receiver said it removed the plugin — it retracted its topics and went offline — but SSH could not confirm it. Disagreed or could not be read: {detail}.
abort.uninstall_reported: The receiver said it removed the plugin: it retracted its topics and went offline. Without stored SSH credentials that is all that can be shown from here.
abort.uninstall_rolled_back: The receiver started the removal but aborted it: {detail}
abort.busy: opkg on the receiver is busy — try again in a few minutes. Nothing was sent.
abort.uninstall_incomplete: The removal did not complete: the receiver retracted its topics and went offline, then came back without saying why. The plugin is most likely still installed; the receiver's last error may say more.
abort.uninstall_no_action: The receiver did not act: nothing in the shape of a removal arrived within a minute. The plugin is most likely still installed; check that the receiver is on and connected.
abort.recording: The receiver is recording. Nothing was sent; try again when the recording has finished.
abort.timer_due: A recording is about to start on the receiver. Nothing was sent; try again later.
abort.mqtt_unavailable: The MQTT integration is not available, so nothing was sent to the receiver.
abort.unknown: Removing the plugin failed unexpectedly; the log has the details.
abort.host_key_changed: The receiver's SSH host key changed and was not accepted.
abort.ssh_unavailable: The receiver's SSH service could not be reached, so nothing was installed.
abort.auth_failed: SSH authentication failed, so nothing was installed.
abort.preflight_failed: The receiver's checks could not be completed, so nothing was installed.
abort.unsupported_python: The receiver's Python version is too old for this plugin. Nothing was installed.
abort.no_space: The receiver does not have enough free space. Nothing was installed.
abort.standby: The receiver is in standby. Installing restarts the receiver's interface, which would wake it and may switch the television on. Nothing was installed; switch the receiver on and try again.
abort.streaming: The receiver is streaming to another device. Installing restarts its interface and would cut the stream off. Nothing was installed; try again when the stream has ended.
abort.bundle_missing: The plugin bundle shipped with this integration is missing. Reinstall the integration.
abort.bundle_invalid: The plugin bundle shipped with this integration failed verification. Reinstall the integration.
abort.upload_failed: The plugin could not be transferred to the receiver. Nothing was changed.
abort.install_failed: The plugin could not be installed. The receiver was put back as it was.
abort.newer_installed: The receiver already runs a newer plugin than this integration ships. Nothing was changed.
abort.provision_failed: The receiver's MQTT settings could not be written. The receiver was put back as it was.
abort.restart_failed: The receiver's interface did not restart safely. The receiver was put back as it was.
abort.announcement_timeout: The plugin did not announce itself after the restart. The receiver was put back as it was.
abort.restart_withdrawn: The receiver asked on screen whether to restart its interface, so the installation was withdrawn: the plugin files on the receiver are as they were before, and nothing was restarted. The question may still be visible on the television - answering "yes" or "no" is safe.
abort.restart_unobserved: The receiver was asked to restart its interface, and the connection to it was lost before the outcome could be seen. Nothing was undone: the new plugin files are on the receiver, and the installer's lock stays on it. Once the lock is thirty minutes old, installing again first puts the previous version back and then installs.
abort.restart_unconfirmed: The receiver did not confirm the request to restart its interface, and its interface did not restart within 60 seconds, so the installation was withdrawn: the plugin files on the receiver are as they were before, and nothing was restarted. If the television shows a question about restarting, answering "yes" or "no" is safe.
abort.withdraw_failed: The receiver's interface did not restart within 60 seconds - usually because the receiver is asking on the television whether to - and putting the previous plugin files back did not complete, so the plugin's files and package records on the receiver may be partly the new ones and partly the previous ones. Nothing was restarted. A question may still be visible on the television: answering "no" keeps the plugin that is running; answering "yes" restarts the interface on the files that are there now, which have not been checked. Install again afterwards.
abort.rollback_unobserved: The installation failed, and the receiver is putting itself back with a script of its own, but the connection to it was lost before that could be seen finishing. The installer's lock stays on the receiver for thirty minutes. If the receiver shows no picture by then, switch it off and on again.
abort.rollback_failed: The installation failed and the receiver could not be put back as it was. Check the receiver by hand: the backup taken before the change is in /home/root/mqttbridge-backups.
abort.rollback_restart_failed: The installation failed and the receiver was put back as it was, but its interface did not start again. Restart the receiver by hand; nothing else needs undoing.
abort.rollback_lock_failed: The receiver was put back as it was, but the installer's transaction lock could not be released. Delete /home/root/mqttbridge-backups/.ha-installer.lock on the receiver, or wait thirty minutes, before installing again.
abort.rollback_opkg_busy: The installation failed, and the receiver could not be put back as it was because its package manager (opkg) stayed busy with another operation — an install or removal from the receiver's own menu, most likely. Nothing was restored. Check the receiver by hand: the backup taken before the change is in /home/root/mqttbridge-backups.
abort.rollback_opkg_overlap: The installation failed and the receiver was put back as it was, but another run of its package manager (opkg) held the lock for part of the restore and may have changed the package database at the same time. Check the receiver by hand (`opkg status enigma2-plugin-extensions-mqttbridge`); the backup taken before the change is in /home/root/mqttbridge-backups.
abort.opkg_busy: The receiver's package manager (opkg) is busy with another operation — an install or removal from the receiver's own menu, or its update check — so nothing was installed. Try again in a minute.
abort.bundle_below_floor: The plugin bundled with this integration, {version}, is below {floor}, the lowest version the plugin's signed release index allows, so nothing was installed. Update this integration to get a newer plugin.
abort.bundle_withdrawn: The plugin bundled with this integration, {version}, has been withdrawn in the plugin's signed release index: {reason}. Nothing was installed. Update this integration to get a newer plugin.
abort.version_below_floor: Plugin {version} is below {floor}, the lowest version the plugin's signed release index allows, so nothing was installed.
abort.version_withdrawn: Plugin {version} has been withdrawn in the plugin's signed release index: {reason}. Nothing was installed.
abort.package_invalid: Could not download plugin {version}, or its checksum does not match the plugin's signed release index. Nothing was changed on the receiver.
abort.depends_missing: Plugin {version} needs packages that are not installed on the receiver: {package}. Nothing was changed.
abort.identity_mismatch: The receiver is configured for node ID {box_node_id} and base topic {box_base_topic}, and the form gives {node_id} and {base_topic}. A value in brackets is one the receiver has not stored, and shows the plugin's default where there is one. Nothing was changed.
abort.downgrade_done: Plugin {version} is installed and running on the receiver. The update card offers the newer release again, because it is still the newest compatible one; skip it there to stay on {version}.
abort.downgrade_not_offered: No older plugin version can be installed on this receiver now: it needs stored SSH credentials, a reported plugin version and a checked list of plugin versions (press “Check for plugin updates”) that lists an older version this integration allows.
abort.version_not_installable: Plugin {version} is no longer a release the plugin's signed release index lets this integration install, so nothing was installed.
abort.busy_stalled: A plugin update on the receiver stopped without finishing and still holds its lock. The lock expires in about {minutes} min; try again then. Nothing was changed.
abort.busy_until: Another installation holds the lock on this receiver: it is still running, or it stopped without releasing the lock. The lock expires in about {minutes} min at the latest; try again then. Nothing was changed.
abort.records_mismatch: The receiver's package records name plugin {recorded}, but the plugin running is {running}: an earlier update did not finish putting the previous version back. Nothing was changed. Reinstall the plugin with “Force plugin reinstall (SSH)” on the device page.
abort.gui_not_answering: The receiver's interface is not answering (OpenWebif is silent), so whether it is recording cannot be checked. The forced reinstall is on hold.
abort.gui_stopped: The receiver's interface was stopped on purpose (runlevel 4). A forced reinstall would start it, so it is on hold.
abort.plugin_not_started: The reinstalled plugin did not start: no new process of the receiver's interface opened its log. The previous state was put back.

progress.uninstalling: Asking the receiver to remove its plugin, and waiting for it to retract its topics and go offline
progress.downgrading: Downloading and checking the older plugin, installing it on the receiver, restarting its interface and waiting for it to announce itself

state.not_supported: Not supported: this receiver cannot be woken over the network from deep standby, only by its remote, its front button or a timer, and on some receivers also by switching on a TV connected over HDMI, if HDMI-CEC is on

Not supported: the magic packet is sent, but this receiver cannot be woken by it from deep standby, only by its remote, its front button or a timer, and on some receivers also by switching on a TV connected over HDMI, if HDMI-CEC is on

trigger_type.list_picked: A row of a list was picked

show_list.name: Show list of choices
show_list.description: Puts a list of choices on the television, on top of whatever is on screen, and the viewer picks one row with the remote. Called with a response, it waits until the list is answered and returns how it ended: ending, row and label. Without one it returns as soon as the list is sent; the answer still fires the device triggers and the event enigma2_mqtt_list_answer.

text.name: Text
text.description: One or two lines under the title, at most 200 characters.

rows.name: Rows
rows.description: 1 to 24 rows, in the order they are shown. Each has an id (1 to 32 letters, digits or . _ : -), which is what the answer says, and a label of at most 60 characters; optionally a key - a colour key or a digit - that picks the row at once, and an icon.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long the list stays on screen, in seconds: 5 to 600. A list always has one.

default.name: Default row
default.description: The id of the row the selection starts on. When the list times out, the answer names this row.

get_recordings.name: Get recordings
get_recordings.description: Returns the receiver's recording library as Home Assistant shows it: its movie locations, their folders and each folder's recordings with their ID, file, title, description, channel, start, length and size. Recordings of the bouquets hidden from “Recently watched” are left out, and so is a folder or a location with nothing left to show. Read from what the receiver has already published; nothing wakes its disk.

delete_recording.name: Delete recording
delete_recording.description: Moves one recording into the receiver's trash. Only for a receiver whose own setting allows it: nothing is ever deleted for good, and with the receiver's trash switched off nothing is deleted at all.

id.name: Recording ID
id.description: The recording's ID: 16 hexadecimal digits, as the receiver's library and the running recordings on “Active recordings” give it.

stop_stream.name: Stop stream
stop_stream.description: Ends one stream the receiver is serving to another device. A player that reconnects by itself opens it again: stopping a client is not blocking it.

host.name: Client address
host.description: The client's address, as the “Stream clients” sensor shows it.

sref.name: Service reference
sref.description: The channel being streamed to that client. Leave empty when the client has one stream open, or to stop the one whose channel the sensor does not show.

zap.name: Zap
zap.description: Tunes the receiver to a channel, by service reference or by name. Give exactly one of the two.

sref.name: Service reference
sref.description: The channel's service reference, trailing colon included. This is the identifier that never changes.

name.name: Channel name
name.description: The channel's name as the bouquet spells it. Refused by the receiver when more than one channel in its configured bouquets has that name.

select_bouquet.name: Select bouquet
select_bouquet.description: Makes a bouquet the receiver's active channel list. Channel up and down then follow that bouquet.

sref.name: Bouquet reference
sref.description: The service reference of a bouquet published by the receiver. If the current channel is outside it, the receiver tunes its first playable channel.

send_key.name: Send key
send_key.description: Injects a remote control key into the receiver, as if somebody had pressed it.

key.name: Key
key.description: The key name, such as `KEY_RED`. `red` works too.

long.name: Long press
long.description: Send it as a held button rather than a tap.

message.name: Show message
message.description: Puts a message on the television: a popup, or a discreet toast in a corner that hides itself. The receiver cuts a popup at 500 characters and a toast at 200.

text.name: Text
text.description: What the popup or toast says.

style.name: Style
style.description: A popup takes focus and waits in the receiver's queue; a toast takes no key press, hides itself and is replaced by the next one. A toast needs a receiver that offers it.

type.name: Type
type.description: Which icon and colour the popup uses.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long the message stays on screen, in seconds. Without one a popup stays 10 seconds and a toast 5; a toast takes 1 to 30.

add_timer.name: Add timer
add_timer.description: Adds a recording timer, either from an EPG event or from a start and end time. Give the event ID, or both times — not both forms.

event_id.name: Event ID
event_id.description: The EPG event to record. Prefer this: the receiver resolves the event itself, so the timer gets the programme's name and the padding the box is set up with.

begin.name: Start
begin.description: When to start recording, for a manual window.

end.name: End
end.description: When to stop recording, for a manual window.

name.name: Name
name.description: What to call the recording, for a manual window.

delete_timer.name: Delete timer
delete_timer.description: Deletes a recording timer. enigma2 identifies a timer by its channel, start and end, so all three are needed.

record.name: Record
record.description: Starts or stops an instant recording of whatever is on.

screenshot.name: Take a screenshot
screenshot.description: Captures what is on the television now and publishes it, which is what refreshes the Screen image entity.

set_ha_mode.name: Set Home Assistant mode
set_ha_mode.description: Switches how the receiver presents itself: through this integration, through MQTT discovery, or not at all. Switching away from integration mode leaves this integration's entities without anything updating them.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Which mode the plugin should run in.

get_epg_grid.name: Get the EPG grid
get_epg_grid.description: Returns what is on, per bouquet, as the receiver last published it. Use it in a template or a script; it is deliberately not an entity attribute, because a grid is tens of kilobytes per bouquet and would be written to the recorder database on every refresh.

bouquet.name: Bouquet
bouquet.description: One bouquet, by name or by slug. Left empty, every published bouquet is returned.

go2rtc_unreachable.title: {name}: go2rtc does not answer
go2rtc_unreachable.description:
Home Assistant keeps the stream “{stream}” of the go2rtc at {host} on the channel {name} is on, as set in the receiver's options. go2rtc did not answer, so that stream still shows an earlier channel, or nothing.

Check that go2rtc is running and that the address in the options is the address of its API (for the go2rtc add-on: port 1984). Home Assistant tries again at the next channel change and every five minutes.

This notice goes away by itself once go2rtc takes the stream again. To stop using go2rtc, empty its address in the receiver's options.

go2rtc_refused.title: {name}: go2rtc refused the stream
go2rtc_refused.description:
The go2rtc at {host} answered HTTP {status} when Home Assistant set its stream “{stream}” to the channel {name} is on, so that stream still shows an earlier channel, or nothing.

Check the source template in the receiver's options: go2rtc refuses a source that contains a space, and a named template used in it has to exist in go2rtc's own configuration. A 401 or 403 means that go2rtc's API asks for a login.

This notice goes away by itself once go2rtc takes the stream again. To stop using go2rtc, empty its address in the receiver's options.

payloads_withheld.title: {name}: the receiver is not publishing everything
payloads_withheld.description:
The plugin on {name} did not publish the following, because each of these messages would exceed the size one MQTT message may have and the broker would close the connection:

{withheld}

In Home Assistant this means: the channels of a bouquet whose list is missing are not offered, and a bouquet without its EPG shows no programmes.

To get them back, limit the bouquets the plugin publishes with its `bouquets_for_select` setting on the receiver (the plugin's setup screen or its OpenWebif page), or split a very large bouquet into smaller ones. Lowering `epg_grid_events` does not bring a missing EPG back: the plugin already shortens it as far as it can before it gives up on it.

This notice goes away by itself once the receiver publishes everything again.

menu_clock_behind.title: {name}: the receiver's clock is behind
menu_clock_behind.description:
{name} sent an action from its Home Assistant menu stamped more than two minutes before Home Assistant's clock, so Home Assistant refused it and did nothing. While the receiver's clock is behind, every OK in that menu is refused.

Set the receiver's clock right: in its time settings, let it take the time from the internet (NTP) or from the transponder, and check its time zone. Check that Home Assistant's own clock is right as well.

This notice goes away by itself at the next action from the menu that Home Assistant accepts.

list_unsupported.message: This receiver cannot show a list of choices. It needs a plugin release that offers one.

list_offline.message: The receiver is not connected to the broker, so it cannot show a list of choices.

list_not_subscribed.message: Home Assistant is not receiving this receiver's answers from the broker yet, so the list was not sent. Try again in a moment.

list_unloaded.message: The receiver was removed from Home Assistant or reloaded before the list was answered.

list_refused.message: The receiver did not show the list: {reason}

list_member_not_text.message: The list's {member} must be a text.

list_rows_not_list.message: The rows must be a list, each row with an id and a label.

list_rows_count.message: A list has {min} to {max} rows; this one has {count}.

list_row_not_mapping.message: Row {row} must have an id and a label.

list_row_member_unknown.message: Row {row} has {member}, which a row does not have. A row has id, label, key and icon.

list_row_member_not_text.message: Row {row}: the {member} must be a text.

list_row_id_invalid.message: Row {row} needs an id of 1 to {max} characters, each a letter, a digit or one of . _ : -

list_row_id_duplicate.message: Row {row} has the id {id}, which an earlier row already has.

list_row_key_invalid.message: Row {row}: the key must be red, green, yellow, blue or a digit from 1 to 9.

list_row_key_duplicate.message: Row {row} has the key {key}, which an earlier row already has.

list_timeout_invalid.message: The timeout must be a whole number of seconds from {min} to {max}.

list_default_unknown.message: The default row must be the id of one of the list's rows.

list_too_long.message: The list takes {size} bytes and the receiver reads at most {limit}. Shorten the labels or the text, or use fewer rows.

list_not_utf8.message: The list holds a character that cannot be sent.

recordings_unsupported.message: This receiver does not publish its recording library: its plugin is older than 0.5.0, or its image does not offer it.

play_recording_busy.message: The plugin is being updated on the receiver. Try again when the update has finished.

delete_recording_busy.message: The plugin is being updated on the receiver. Try again when the update has finished.

recordings_refresh_busy.message: The plugin is being updated on the receiver. Try again when the update has finished.

play_recording_timeshift_kept.message: The viewer chose to keep timeshift when the receiver asked, so the recording was not played.

delete_recording_in_progress.message: The receiver is still moving another recording to its trash. Try again in a moment.

recording_delete_not_ready.message: Deleting is allowed on the receiver and its trash is on, but the receiver does not offer it yet: its plugin has not read the recording library since it started. Try again in a moment.

recording_id_invalid.message: A recording's ID is 16 hexadecimal digits.

recording_unknown.message: The receiver's library does not list a recording with the ID {id}. It may have been deleted, or be one of the oldest recordings of a folder too large to list whole.

recording_play_unsupported.message: This receiver cannot play a recording from Home Assistant: its plugin is older than 0.5.0, or its image does not offer it.

recording_receiver_offline.message: The receiver is not connected to the broker, so nothing was sent.

recording_other_receiver.message: That recording belongs to another receiver. Play it on that receiver's media player.

recording_plays_on_receiver.message: A recording is played by the receiver itself, on its television. Choose the receiver's own media player to play it.

recording_delete_not_permitted.message: Deleting recordings from Home Assistant is switched off on the receiver. It can only be switched on in the plugin's settings on the receiver itself.

recording_delete_trash_off.message: The receiver's trash is switched off, so nothing is deleted: a recording deleted from Home Assistant only ever goes to the receiver's trash. Switch the trash on in the receiver's settings.

recording_delete_unsupported.message: This receiver cannot delete a recording from Home Assistant: its plugin is older than 0.5.0, or its image has no trash.

delete_recording_in_use.message: That recording is being recorded or played, and cannot be deleted now.

delete_recording_not_permitted.message: Deleting recordings from Home Assistant is switched off on the receiver. It can only be switched on in the plugin's settings on the receiver itself.

delete_recording_trash_off.message: The receiver's trash is switched off, so nothing is deleted: a recording deleted from Home Assistant only ever goes to the receiver's trash. Switch the trash on in the receiver's settings.

delete_recording_not_in_library.message: The receiver's library does not list that recording any more.

delete_recording_file_gone.message: The recording's file is no longer on the receiver.

play_recording_not_in_library.message: The receiver's library does not list that recording any more.

play_recording_file_gone.message: The recording's file is no longer on the receiver.

menu_transparency_step.message: {value} % is not a menu transparency the receiver takes: it takes 0 to 80 % in steps of 10.

menu_combo_presses_step.message: {value} is not a number of presses the receiver takes: it takes 2 to 5.

menu_combo_gap_step.message: {value} s is not a gap the receiver takes: it takes 0.3 to 3.0 s in steps of 0.1 s.

stream_source_unknown.message: That receiver, bouquet or channel is not offered for streaming here. Open the media browser again and pick from what is there now.

stream_player_browser.message: The browser cannot play a receiver's transport stream. Choose a media player that decodes it itself, such as Kodi, VLC or an Android TV player.

stream_player_cast.message: Chromecast cannot play a receiver's transport stream. Choose a media player that decodes it itself, such as Kodi, VLC or an Android TV player.

stream_login_required.message: The receiver's stream server asks for a login, and Home Assistant never puts a login into a stream address. Switch the login off in the receiver's streaming settings to play its channels from here.

stream_no_address.message: Home Assistant has no address at which to reach the receiver's stream server. Enter the receiver's host with Reconfigure.

stream_no_facts.message: The receiver has a stream server but has published nothing usable about it yet. Check that the plugin is running: it publishes where its stream server is every time it connects.

stream_not_playable.message: {channel} cannot be streamed right now: the tuner it needs is in use by the television, a recording or another stream.

stream_stop_unsupported.message: This receiver cannot stop a stream client: its image's stream server does not offer it, or the plugin is older than 0.5.0.

stream_client_unknown.message: No stream client with the address {host} is on the receiver's list.

stream_client_ambiguous.message: {host} has more than one stream open. Give the service reference of the one to stop.

stream_client_hidden_ambiguous.message: {host} has more than one stream open on channels of hidden bouquets, and their service references are shown nowhere. Stop them on the receiver, or show the bouquet again in the options.

stream_stop_not_connected.message: That stream client is no longer connected to the receiver.

stream_stop_not_stopped.message: The receiver did not stop that stream client.

mqtt_not_available.message: The MQTT integration is not available, so the receiver cannot be reached.

command_timeout.message: The receiver did not carry out `{command}`. Check that it is on and that the plugin is running.

zap_needs_one.message: Give either a service reference or a channel name, not both and not neither.

timer_needs_event_or_window.message: A timer needs either an event ID or both a start and an end time.

timer_takes_one_form.message: Give an event ID or a start and end time, not both.

unknown_bouquet.message: The receiver has published no EPG grid for the bouquet {bouquet}.

bouquet_not_published.message: The receiver does not offer the bouquet {bouquet}.

toast_unsupported.message: This receiver does not offer the discreet toast. Switch it on in the plugin's settings on the receiver, or update the plugin, or send a popup instead.

toast_timeout_out_of_range.message: A toast hides itself, so its timeout must be {min} to {max} seconds, not {timeout}.

bouquet_context_unsupported.message: This receiver plugin cannot activate a bouquet context. Update the plugin to use this action.

unknown_channel.message: No channel called {channel} is in the bouquets this receiver offers.

unsupported_media_type.message: A receiver can play a channel, not {media_type}.

wake_on_lan_unavailable.message: The Wake on LAN integration is not set up, so no magic packet can be sent. Add it from Settings, then try again.

no_mac.message: This receiver has not reported a MAC address, so there is nowhere to send a magic packet. Set one in the integration's options.

update_version_unknown.message: The receiver has not reported its installed plugin version.

update_downgrade.message: Refusing to replace a newer plugin with an older version: the update card never installs an older one.

update_version_unavailable.message: The requested version is neither the bundled plugin nor a release the plugin's signed index lets this integration install.

update_version_below_floor.message: Plugin version {version} is below {floor}, the lowest version the plugin's signed index allows.

release_check_unverified.message: The list of plugin versions could not be verified; it may have been changing while it was read. Try again in a few minutes. Nothing was changed.

release_check_rate_limited.message: Versions were checked at {time}. The next check is possible in {minutes} min.

release_check_refused.message: The list of plugin versions has an invalid signature or is older than the one already known. Nothing was changed.

release_check_failed.message: The list of plugin versions could not be fetched ({reason}). Nothing was changed.

release_check_bad_memory.message: The stored record of accepted plugin version lists cannot be read, so no new list is accepted. To start again, delete .storage/enigma2_mqtt.release_index in Home Assistant's configuration directory.

update_no_credentials.message: No SSH credentials are stored for this receiver. Reconfigure it and tick “Keep SSH credentials for updates”, then try again.

update_withdrawn.message: The receiver asked on screen whether to restart its interface, so the update was withdrawn; the previous version of the plugin is running. The question may still be visible on the television - answering "yes" or "no" is safe.

update_standby.message: The receiver is in standby. Updating restarts the receiver's interface, which would wake it and may switch the television on. Switch the receiver on and try again.

update_streaming.message: The receiver is streaming to another device. Updating restarts its interface and would cut the stream off. Try again when the stream has ended.

update_restart_unobserved.message: The receiver was asked to restart its interface, and the connection to it was lost before the outcome could be seen. Nothing was undone, and the installer's lock stays on the receiver. Once it is thirty minutes old, updating again first puts the previous plugin version back.

update_rollback_unobserved.message: The update failed, and the receiver is putting the previous version back with a script of its own, but the connection to it was lost before that could be seen finishing. The installer's lock stays on the receiver for thirty minutes. If the receiver shows no picture by then, switch it off and on again.

update_restart_unconfirmed.message: The receiver did not confirm the request to restart its interface, and its interface did not restart within 60 seconds, so the update was withdrawn; the previous version of the plugin is running. If the television shows a question about restarting, answering "yes" or "no" is safe.

update_withdraw_failed.message: The receiver's interface did not restart within 60 seconds - usually because the receiver is asking on the television whether to - and putting the previous plugin files back did not complete, so the plugin's files and package records on the receiver may be partly the new ones and partly the previous ones. Nothing was restarted. A question may still be visible on the television: answering "no" keeps the version that is running; answering "yes" restarts the interface on the files that are there now, which have not been checked. Update again afterwards.

channel_not_in_active_bouquet.message: {channel} is not in the bouquet the receiver is on, so the source list does not offer it. Switch the “Bouquet” select to the bouquet it belongs to first, or use the enigma2_mqtt.zap action, which takes a service reference and is not scoped.

option_no_longer_offered.message: {option} is no longer on this list. The receiver republished its channels while it was being chosen; open the list again and pick from what is there now.

history_clear_standby.message: The receiver is in standby, where 0 does not clear its zap history.

history_clear_panic_off.message: The receiver's panic-button setting is off, so 0 only goes back to the previous channel and clears nothing.

history_clear_too_short.message: The receiver's zap history holds at most one channel — there is nothing to clear.

history_clear_timeshift.message: Timeshift is running — the receiver would ask on screen whether to leave it. Leave timeshift and try again.

history_clear_zap_blocked.message: The receiver is holding zaps for a moment after timeshift. Try again in a few seconds.

history_clear_pip.message: Picture-in-picture is showing and 0 is set to act on it, so the history would not be cleared.

history_clear_playback.message: A recording is being played back. Stop it and try again.

history_clear_not_cleared.message: The receiver did not clear its zap history.

history_clear_screen_open.message: A menu, the channel list or the EPG is open on the receiver's screen, where 0 would not reach the history. Close it and try again.

zap_history_playback.message: The receiver is playing back a recording, where its zap history is not on screen. Stop the playback and try again.

update_download_failed.message: Could not download plugin {version}, or its checksum does not match the plugin's signed release index. Nothing was changed on the receiver.

update_depends_missing.message: Plugin {version} needs packages that are not installed on the receiver: {package}. Nothing was changed.

relay_no_ipv4.message: The receiver did not report an IPv4 address, so Home Assistant cannot share the plugin with it safely.

relay_no_address.message: Home Assistant does not know its address on the local network. Set “Local network” in Home Assistant's network settings.

relay_busy.message: Home Assistant is sending this receiver the plugin right now. Try again when that download has finished.

relay_unreachable.message: The receiver could not download the plugin from Home Assistant ({url}). Set Home Assistant's “Local network” address to one the receiver can reach.

relay_not_downloaded.message: Home Assistant offered plugin {version} to the receiver at {url}, but it was not downloaded within ten minutes. If an install on the receiver failed, check that the receiver can reach this address.

update_busy_stalled.message: A plugin update on the receiver stopped without finishing and still holds its lock. The lock expires in about {minutes} min; try again then. Nothing was changed.

update_busy_until.message: Another installation holds the lock on this receiver: it is still running, or it stopped without releasing the lock. The lock expires in about {minutes} min at the latest; try again then. Nothing was changed.

update_records_mismatch.message: The receiver's package records name plugin {recorded}, but the plugin running is {running}: an earlier update did not finish putting the previous version back. Nothing was changed. Reinstall the plugin with “Force plugin reinstall (SSH)” on the device page.

update_mqtt_not_permitted.message: The receiver refused: updates over MQTT are switched off in the plugin's settings on the receiver. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_no_capability.message: The plugin on the receiver was not installed by its package manager, so it cannot update itself. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_busy.message: The receiver is already installing, updating or removing the plugin.

update_mqtt_opkg_busy.message: The receiver's package manager is busy. Nothing was changed; try again in a few minutes.

update_mqtt_recording.message: The receiver is recording or will start recording soon. Try again when the recording has finished.

update_mqtt_recording_unknown.message: The receiver could not say whether a recording is due, so it did not update. Nothing was changed; try again later.

update_mqtt_epg_import.message: An EPG import is running on the receiver. Try again when it has finished.

update_mqtt_cannot_restart.message: The receiver's image offers no way to restart its interface, so the plugin cannot update itself there. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_bad_request.message: The receiver could not read the update request. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_unknown_version.message: The receiver's own signed list of plugin versions does not include {version}. Nothing was changed. Home Assistant passes its newer list on to the receiver; try again in a minute.

update_mqtt_withdrawn.message: The receiver refused plugin {version}: its signed list of versions marks it withdrawn. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_below_floor.message: The receiver refused plugin {version}: it is below the lowest version its signed list of versions allows. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_incompatible.message: The receiver refused plugin {version} as not compatible with its plugin or with this integration. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_depends.message: Plugin {version} needs a package that is not installed on the receiver. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_current.message: Plugin {version} is already installed and running on the receiver. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_checksum.message: The receiver's signed list of versions gives plugin {version} a different checksum from Home Assistant's. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_relay.message: The receiver did not accept Home Assistant's download address: the address is not one it can use, or the receiver's clock says it has already expired. Check the receiver's clock, and Home Assistant's local network address (Settings > System > Network). Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_no_space.message: There is not enough free space on the receiver for the update. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_rate_limited.message: An update ran on the receiver less than ten minutes ago. Try again later.

update_mqtt_no_relay.message: The receiver cannot reach the plugin's release origin and Home Assistant did not answer, so the update started on the receiver could not be installed. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_clock_skew.message: The receiver got a download address that its clock already calls expired. If the receiver's clock is wrong, set it and try again. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_unreachable.message: The receiver could not get a signed list of plugin versions. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_snapshot_failed.message: The receiver could not copy the current plugin to roll back to, so it did not update. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_opkg_failed.message: The receiver's package manager could not install plugin {version}. The receiver put the previous plugin files back.

update_mqtt_manifest.message: The installed plugin {version} did not match its own list of files, so the receiver put the previous version back.

update_mqtt_internal_error.message: An unexpected error on the receiver stopped the update. The previous plugin version is still in place.

update_mqtt_restore_failed.message: The update failed and the receiver could not put the previous plugin files back. Reinstall the plugin with “Force plugin reinstall (SSH)” on the device page.

update_mqtt_restore_failed_manual.message: The update failed and the receiver could not put the previous plugin files back. Install the plugin on the receiver again by hand, as for a first installation (see the integration's documentation).

update_mqtt_restore_incomplete.message: The update failed; the previous plugin version is back, but not all of its package records. Reinstall the plugin with “Force plugin reinstall (SSH)” on the device page.

update_mqtt_restore_incomplete_manual.message: The update failed; the previous plugin version is back, but not all of its package records. Install the plugin on the receiver again by hand, as for a first installation (see the integration's documentation).

update_mqtt_not_stopped.message: The update was rolled back while the receiver's interface kept running, so the plugin's files are no longer the ones it runs. Restart the receiver's interface.

update_mqtt_interface_not_started.message: The update was rolled back, but the receiver's interface did not start again. Switch the receiver off and on again at its power switch.

update_mqtt_time_limit.message: The update ran out of time before the receiver restarted its interface; the previous plugin version stays.

update_mqtt_interrupted.message: The update was interrupted on the receiver before the plugin was replaced. Nothing was changed.

update_mqtt_interrupted_files_reinstall.message: The update was interrupted on the receiver after its package manager had started replacing the plugin's files, so they may now be a mix of two versions. Reinstall the plugin with “Force plugin reinstall (SSH)” on the device page.

update_mqtt_interrupted_files_manual.message: The update was interrupted on the receiver after its package manager had started replacing the plugin's files, so they may now be a mix of two versions. Install the plugin on the receiver again by hand, as for a first installation (see the integration's documentation).

update_mqtt_interrupted_unknown_reinstal.message: The update was interrupted on the receiver, and Home Assistant cannot tell whether the plugin's files had already been changed. If the receiver's “Last error” sensor says the plugin must be installed again, use “Force plugin reinstall (SSH)” on the device page.

update_mqtt_interrupted_unknown_manual.message: The update was interrupted on the receiver, and Home Assistant cannot tell whether the plugin's files had already been changed. If the receiver's “Last error” sensor says the plugin must be installed again, install it by hand, as for a first installation (see the integration's documentation).

update_mqtt_interrupted_signal.message: The update was interrupted on the receiver, and the plugin's previous version stays: its files were not changed, or were put back whole. Nothing needs to be done.

update_mqtt_interrupted_lock.message: The update was interrupted on the receiver because another process took its lock. The plugin's files are whole — the previous version or the new one. If the receiver's “Last error” sensor asks for it, restart the receiver's interface.

update_mqtt_reloaded.message: Home Assistant reloaded the integration while the update was running, so this request no longer follows it. The card shows the receiver's progress.

update_mqtt_replaced.message: The receiver stopped reporting this update, and the plugin it runs now, {running}, was installed by something else in the meantime. Whether this update changed anything is not known. Check the plugin version on the receiver, and update again if version {version} is still wanted.

update_mqtt_download.message: The receiver could not download the plugin from Home Assistant ({url}). Check that the receiver can reach Home Assistant on the local network.

update_mqtt_question.message: The receiver did not restart its interface (the question on screen was answered “no”, or nobody answered). The update was withdrawn.

update_mqtt_retraction.message: The update was withdrawn before the restart because the receiver's topics could not be cleared in time. The previous plugin version is running.

update_mqtt_withdrawn_standby.message: The receiver went into standby before its interface restarted, so the update was withdrawn. The previous plugin version is running.

update_mqtt_withdrawn_recording.message: A recording started or is due on the receiver, so the update was withdrawn before the restart. The previous plugin version is running.

update_mqtt_withdrawn_epg_import.message: An EPG import started on the receiver, so the update was withdrawn before the restart. The previous plugin version is running.

update_mqtt_withdrawn_before_restart.message: The update was withdrawn before the receiver's interface restarted. The previous plugin version is running.

update_mqtt_not_started.message: The new version of the plugin did not start. The receiver put the previous version {from_version} back.

update_mqtt_rolled_back_time_limit.message: The update ran out of time and was undone, which says nothing against the release itself. The receiver put the previous version {from_version} back.

update_mqtt_rolled_back_interrupted.message: The update was interrupted after the new files were installed, so the receiver put the previous version {from_version} back.

update_mqtt_drill.message: The acceptance drill rolled the update back on purpose. The receiver put the previous version {from_version} back.

update_mqtt_rolled_back.message: The update was undone, and the receiver put the previous version {from_version} back.

update_mqtt_failed.message: The plugin update on the receiver failed: {error}

update_mqtt_refused.message: The receiver refused the plugin update: {error}

update_mqtt_no_answer.message: The receiver did not answer the update request within a minute. If it starts the update after all, its progress appears on this card; the download address stays valid for ten minutes.

update_mqtt_still_running.message: The update is still running on the receiver.

update_mqtt_unproven.message: The receiver reports the update installed, but it runs plugin {running} rather than the signed build of {version}. Check the plugin version on the receiver.

update_mqtt_release_only.message: Over MQTT the receiver installs only releases from the plugin's signed release index, and {version} is not one of them. Nothing was changed.
